author: rule-family designer (world: a 5x5 picture of black and white squares; lineup answer)
description: 5x5-PICTURE RULE-FAMILY class, REVISION 2 = LINEUP ANSWER (docs/RULE_FAMILIES.md sec. 'Revision 2'; working notes in challenges/lab/NOTES_rules_pixels.md, v1 kept as challenges/lab/ospren.v1.json). CLUE LAYOUT, blocks separated by ONE BLANK LINE: first 2 or 3 EXAMPLE pictures, each five lines of five characters from '#' (black) and '.' (white); then FOUR CANDIDATE blocks, each a line holding just its number 1..4 followed by the five lines of that candidate. A block of five picture lines is an example; a block of six lines whose first line is a digit is a candidate; the candidates are always the last four blocks. ANSWER = the one candidate that obeys the hidden rule, written back verbatim (whitespace-insensitive, with or without its number line) or as its 1-based index 1..4. Exactly one candidate obeys the rule, checked in generate on every clue (500/500). THE V1 FRESH-COUNT AND >=2-SQUARES CLAUSES ARE GONE, as revision 2 requires: nothing about the answer has to be 'fresh' any more, because the lineup does that work - no candidate is one of the examples (500/500) and the four are always distinct. WHY: ospren v1 was never played, but the same construction attack that took 77-97% off dornic/tresk/tavrik v1 applies verbatim to a picture world - keep every predicate of a 300-strong pool that is true of all the examples and draw a picture satisfying them all at once, and the hidden rule is satisfied by construction. A choice among four kills it: the intersection has nothing to intersect. UNIVERSE U: unchanged from v1 - 10 templates, 29 rules over a 15-number readout of a picture (blacks; same in a left-right mirror; same flipped top-to-bottom; same turned upside down; black corners; rows used; columns used; blobs joined side by side; completely black rows; completely black columns; middle square black; every row the same number; every column the same number; biggest blob; black squares standing alone). COUNT exactly n blacks n=5,6,7; SYM mirror / flip / half turn; CORNERS exactly n corners black n=1..4; SPREAD the blacks sit in exactly n rows or n columns n=1,2; BLOBS exactly n blobs n=1..4; FULLLINE exactly one row / exactly one column completely black; MIDDLE the middle square is black; EQLINE every row / every column the same number; MAXBLOB the biggest blob is n squares n=2,3,4; LONELY exactly n blacks stand completely alone n=3,4,5. 21 of the 29 may be the HIDDEN rule (density <= 0.20 on a naive random picture); the other 8 - the three COUNT rules, 1 and 2 black corners, 3 and 4 blobs and MIDDLE - stay in U as COMPETITORS the generator must kill, which still forces the clue's layout for free: the COUNT rules can only die if the examples disagree about the number of blacks (500/500 distinct counts), MIDDLE only if some example has a white middle and another a black one. U IS AN ANTICHAIN (0 nesting violations over the picture pool) - see v1 for the casualties of that check. WHAT CHANGED INSIDE U'S USE: the template is still drawn BEFORE its parameter, but the eight eligible templates are no longer equally likely. Measured rarity-weighted attack per template - spread 70%, corners 60%, eqline 51%, fullline 47%, sym 43%, maxblob 40%, lonely 33%, blobs 30% - so the weights lean toward the DERIVED readouts (blobs, lonely squares, biggest blob), which have to be read off a picture in two steps and which a decoy can therefore be built to imitate; that is RULE_FAMILIES.md sec. 5c's finding, and it is a difficulty dial rather than a pool-specific hack. Mix over 500 clues: blobs 83, maxblob 78, lonely 76, fullline 75, sym 74, eqline 43, spread 36, corners 35; all 21 eligible rules appear over 2000 seeds (2 blobs 202 ... 1 column 27). THE LINEUP (revision-2 rules 1-5, 5b, 5c): exactly one candidate obeys R; all four have the SAME NUMBER OF BLACK SQUARES (500/500), which makes every count-shaped statement - and the three count-shaped traps - matched for free; all four fire EXACTLY THE SAME example-consistent excluded rules (MATCHED TRAP PROFILES, sec. 5b: 500/500), so every trap heuristic and any count of traps is worth exactly 25.0%; every decoy fails R and fires at least one consistent trap (500/500); none of the four is an example and all four are distinct (500/500 each); the true candidate's position is uniform (139/124/127/110). DECOYS VS THE POOL: since no player has played ospren, generate carries a 300-predicate pool of the kind the round-1 winner built for the other worlds (zpools.py style) - every count a picture has and every at-least / at-most bound on it, per row, per column, corners, border, middle 3x3, blobs, lonely squares, touching pairs, full and empty lines, the five symmetries, runs, rectangles, parities - plus a base rate for each measured on the generator's own 16000-picture pool. It scores every candidate BOTH ways, by the plain count of the surviving predicates it satisfies and by their rarity-weighted total (-log base rate), and aims the true candidate's RANK on both readings at a place drawn uniformly from the 16 (count rank, rarity rank) squares, falling back through the rest in order of distance; decoys are drawn at random, TARGETED at the tight surviving predicates through a per-predicate index, and finally chosen from the near or far end of their distance order from the truth so that 'the odd one out' is aimed too. RESULT over 500 fresh clues (seeds 1e6..1e6+499): 'pick the candidate satisfying the most surviving pool predicates' - the direct port of the round-1 attack - scores 31.6% (floor 25%), with at least one decoy strictly out-counting the truth on 68.4% of clues (revision-2 rule 2 asks for >= 40%); 'fewest' 23.4%, so the count is not reversible. HONEST LIMITS, the two named residues: (i) the RARITY-WEIGHTED version of the same attack still scores 46.8% on the 500-clue table (42.5% over 2000 seeds; the count attack is 29.1% there) - on the clues where the hidden rule is itself a predicate of the pool, and this pool can express most of U, it is the rarest thing all the examples share and no decoy can look as specially chosen; the template re-weighting above took this from 47% to 43% and preferring two-example clues took it from 58%; (ii) 'pick the candidate least like the other three' scores 32.2% (medoid 13.6%) - a picture that obeys a structural rule is genuinely a little unlike three that do not, and the near/far decoy selection only halves that tell. EXAMPLE-SET CHOICE, the one real change to the clue's logic: generate builds up to four minimal example sets of each size and prefers the one leaving the most RARE outside predicates alive, because those are the coincidences a decoy can be built to carry. Two-example sets win that criterion almost always (2 examples 90.5%, 3 examples 9.4% over 2000 seeds; v1 was 52/48), and the measurement behind the choice is blunt: with the example set drawn without that preference, a decoy could out-score the truth on only 19% of three-example clues against 62% of two-example ones (mean rare surviving predicates 3.8 vs 5.8) - a third example removes exactly the coincidences the decoys need. With the preference in place the three-example clues that survive are the good ones: over 2000 seeds the rarity attack scores 41.4% on two-example clues and 53.2% on the 9% that carry three. Uniqueness and minimality inside U are unchanged and still verified on every clue. DEMOTION CHECK (asked for explicitly): no template had to be demoted to competitor-only. The tavrik failure mode - a template whose loose cousins' CONJUNCTION is the rule, so that no decoy can share the truth's trap profile - needs a matched at-least / at-most pair among the exclusions, and ospren has exactly one such pair ('at least n blacks' / 'at most n blacks', fitted to the clue's smallest and biggest); their conjunction is a RANGE, never a single count, because the examples always disagree about the number of blacks, and COUNT is a competitor-only template anyway. Empirically: a matched-profile lineup was found on 500/500 clues and all 21 eligible rules are drawn. DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED (never in U; learning what this class never says is the game), with the rate at which the trap fitted to the clue is consistent with EVERY example and what a player who always picks a candidate satisfying it scores: every square that is black in all the examples is black 100% / 25.0%; at least n black squares 100% / 25.0%; at most n black squares 100% / 25.0%; the same number of blacks as an example 100% / 25.0%; there is a black in the middle column 56.4% / 25.0%; the middle square is white 49.0% / 25.0%; every row has at least one black 33.8% / 25.0%; as many blacks above the middle row as below 30.8% / 25.0%; as many blacks left of the middle column as right 24.2% / 25.0%; the four corners are all the same colour 19.6% / 25.0%; the top row is the same as the bottom row 14.2% / 25.0%; the first column is the same as the last 10.6% / 25.0%; the top row is all white 5.8% / 25.0%; no two black squares touch 2.8% / 25.0%. All fourteen are EXACTLY 25.0% by construction - in v1 they paid 9-19%. Mean 6.5 of them are consistent with any one clue (min 4, max 10). The class only ever makes TIGHT statements about BLACK squares (exactly three corners, the biggest blob IS four, EVERY row the SAME number, the picture IS its own mirror) and never loose ones (at least, at most, no two touching, there is a..., the top row is white). WITNESSES over 500 fresh clues: the true rule (solve) 100%; the IN-U INTERSECTION - the candidate satisfying every rule of U the examples allow - 100%; a player who knows U minus its two rarest templates (spread, corners) 89.4%, minus sym+eqline 81.8%, minus blobs+lonely 74.6%; a player whose universe is U plus the 14 exclusions, committing to a random survivor, 35.0%, to a WRONG survivor 24.4%; MOST surviving pool predicates weighted by rarity 46.8%; the candidate least like the other three 32.2%; MOST surviving pool predicates 31.6%; least like an example 29.0%; pick candidate 1 27.8%; most fitted traps 26.8%; most like an example 23.8%; FEWEST pool predicates 23.4%; fewest fitted traps 23.4%; a random candidate 22.4%; each of the 14 excluded rules exactly 25.0%; the candidate closest to the other three 13.6%. MEASURED over 500 clues: uniqueness 500/500, minimality 500/500, distinct example counts 500/500, examples pairwise >= 3 squares apart 2000/2000, exactly one candidate obeys R 500/500, same number of blacks 500/500, four distinct candidates 500/500, no candidate equal to an example 500/500, matched trap profiles 500/500, every decoy fires a consistent trap 500/500. Clue 192-223 chars, answer 29 chars (or 1). generate 2.39 ms mean / 1.11 ms median / 12.5 ms p99 / 17.9 ms max over 5000 seeds (cap 100); the 16000-picture pool with its 29-bit U mask, 10-bit trap mask, 25-bit square mask and 300-bit attacker-pool mask costs about 4.3 s once per worker at module level and is not charged to max_generate_ms; solve 0.11 ms mean; score 0.07 ms mean. generate is deterministic across processes and hash seeds (md5 of the first 200 clues checked in three interpreters). SCORE is 899 chars (v1: 1004; needs max_score_code_chars = 1024, the raise RULE_FAMILIES.md sec.4 allows for this paradigm): it splits the clue on blank lines, takes the last four blocks as the lineup, resolves the answer to one of them (verbatim, whitespace-insensitive, with or without the number line, or an index 1..4), rebuilds all 29 rules of U from a 58-character table, filters them by the examples, insists on a single survivor and asks whether the chosen candidate obeys it. Checked on 500 clues x every candidate and x every index (exactly one scores 1 each time) and rejects '', 'x', '0', '5', '9', '1 2', '1'x100, '#'x4000, the clue, the example block alone, a unicode digit, a well-formed picture not in the lineup, and the true candidate with one square rubbed out. No hidden channel. SOLVE re-derives the survivor exactly as the scorer does and returns the true candidate verbatim - it constructs nothing, so there is nothing to leak.

# --- world: a 5x5 picture of black ('#') and white ('.') squares ---------------------------
def RP(rng):
    """A varied random 5x5 picture with 2..15 black squares (None if out of range)."""
    m = rng.randrange(9)
    S = set()
    if m == 0:                                             # plain scatter
        S = set(divmod(i, 5) for i in rng.sample(range(25), rng.randint(2, 15)))
    elif m in (1, 2, 3):                                   # a symmetric picture
        p = rng.choice((0.2, 0.3, 0.45))
        for r in range(5):
            for c in range(5):
                if rng.random() < p:
                    S.add((r, c))
                    S.add((r, 4 - c) if m == 1 else (4 - r, c) if m == 2 else (4 - r, 4 - c))
    elif m == 4:                                           # one to three grown blobs
        for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
            cur = {(rng.randrange(5), rng.randrange(5))}
            for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 6)):
                r, c = rng.choice(sorted(cur))
                d = rng.choice(((1, 0), (-1, 0), (0, 1), (0, -1)))
                p = (r + d[0], c + d[1])
                if 0 <= p[0] < 5 and 0 <= p[1] < 5:
                    cur.add(p)
            S |= cur
    elif m == 5:                                           # the same count in every row / column
        k = rng.randint(1, 3)
        tr = rng.random() < 0.5
        for i in range(5):
            for j in rng.sample(range(5), k):
                S.add((i, j) if tr else (j, i))
    elif m == 6:                                           # everything inside one to three lines
        tr = rng.random() < 0.5
        for i in rng.sample(range(5), rng.randint(1, 3)):
            for j in rng.sample(range(5), rng.randint(1, 5)):
                S.add((i, j) if tr else (j, i))
    elif m == 7:                                           # a planted full line + scatter
        tr = rng.random() < 0.5
        i = rng.randrange(5)
        for j in range(5):
            S.add((i, j) if tr else (j, i))
        for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 6)):
            S.add((rng.randrange(5), rng.randrange(5)))
    elif rng.random() < 0.5:                               # planted corners
        for p in ((0, 0), (0, 4), (4, 0), (4, 4)):
            if rng.random() < 0.8:
                S.add(p)
        for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 6)):
            S.add((rng.randrange(5), rng.randrange(5)))
    else:                                                  # sparse, nothing touching
        for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 8)):
            p = (rng.randrange(5), rng.randrange(5))
            if not any((p[0] + d[0], p[1] + d[1]) in S for d in ((1, 0), (-1, 0), (0, 1), (0, -1))):
                S.add(p)
    if not 2 <= len(S) <= 15:
        return None
    return tuple("".join("#" if (r, c) in S else "." for c in range(5)) for r in range(5))


def FT(g):
    """The 15-number readout of a picture. Every rule of U is one of these == a constant."""
    R = [r.count("#") for r in g]
    C = [sum(r[i] == "#" for r in g) for i in range(5)]
    S = set((r, c) for r in range(5) for c in range(5) if g[r][c] == "#")
    Z = []
    while S:                                               # blob sizes (squares joined side by side)
        q = [S.pop()]
        z = 0
        while q:
            r, c = q.pop()
            z += 1
            for p in ((r + 1, c), (r - 1, c), (r, c + 1), (r, c - 1)):
                if p in S:
                    S.discard(p)
                    q.append(p)
        Z.append(z)
    g = list(g)
    return [sum(R),                                        # 0  how many black squares
            g == [r[::-1] for r in g],                     # 1  same in a left-right mirror
            g == g[::-1],                                  # 2  same flipped top-to-bottom
            g == [r[::-1] for r in g[::-1]],               # 3  same turned upside down
            (g[0][0] + g[0][4] + g[4][0] + g[4][4]).count("#"),   # 4  black corners
            sum(x > 0 for x in R),                         # 5  rows that hold a black
            sum(x > 0 for x in C),                         # 6  columns that hold a black
            len(Z),                                        # 7  blobs
            R.count(5),                                    # 8  completely black rows
            C.count(5),                                    # 9  completely black columns
            g[2][2] == "#",                                # 10 the middle square
            len(set(R)) == 1,                              # 11 every row the same number
            len(set(C)) == 1,                              # 12 every column the same number
            max(Z + [0]),                                  # 13 the biggest blob
            Z.count(1)]                                    # 14 black squares standing alone


def UNIV():
    """U: 10 templates, 29 rules. (i, v) means readout number i equals v."""
    U  = [(0, n) for n in (5, 6, 7)]              # COUNT     exactly n black squares  (competitor)
    U += [(1, 1), (2, 1), (3, 1)]                 # SYM       mirror / flip / half turn
    U += [(4, n) for n in (1, 2, 3, 4)]           # CORNERS   exactly n black corners  (1,2 competitor)
    U += [(5, 1), (5, 2), (6, 1), (6, 2)]         # SPREAD    the blacks use exactly n rows / columns
    U += [(7, n) for n in (1, 2, 3, 4)]           # BLOBS     exactly n blobs          (3,4 competitor)
    U += [(8, 1), (9, 1)]                         # FULLLINE  exactly one row / column all black
    U += [(10, 1)]                                # MIDDLE    the middle square is black (competitor)
    U += [(11, 1), (12, 1)]                       # EQLINE    every row / column the same number
    U += [(13, n) for n in (2, 3, 4)]             # MAXBLOB   the biggest blob is n squares
    U += [(14, n) for n in (3, 4, 5)]             # LONELY    exactly n blacks stand alone
    return U


# ---- the OUTSIDE predicate pool the lineup is built to defeat ------------------------------
# No player has played ospren yet, so this is the pool a strong Opus player WOULD enumerate
# about a 5x5 picture, written in the style of the round-1 winner's zpools.py (team dornic1b):
# every count a picture has (per row, per column, corners, edge, middle, blobs, lonely squares,
# touching pairs), every at-least / at-most bound on them, the five symmetries, the run and
# rectangle shapes, and the parities.  300 predicates.  They are written over the picture's
# readout FE(g) rather than over the raw picture only so the module-level table is affordable;
# each is still a single natural sentence a player would think of.
def ospren_preds():
    P = {}
    def a(n, f): P[n] = f
    # ---- how many black squares, and every bound on it
    for k in range(26):
        a('n=%d' % k, (lambda k: (lambda f: f['n'] == k))(k))
    for k in range(1, 21):
        a('n>=%d' % k, (lambda k: (lambda f: f['n'] >= k))(k))
        a('n<=%d' % k, (lambda k: (lambda f: f['n'] <= k))(k))
    a('neven', lambda f: f['n'] % 2 == 0)
    a('nodd', lambda f: f['n'] % 2 == 1)
    for k in (3, 4, 5):
        a('ndiv%d' % k, (lambda k: (lambda f: f['n'] % k == 0))(k))
    a('nprime', lambda f: f['n'] in (2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19, 23))
    # ---- how many in each row and each column
    for i in range(5):
        for k in range(6):
            a('row%d=%d' % (i, k), (lambda i, k: (lambda f: f['R'][i] == k))(i, k))
            a('col%d=%d' % (i, k), (lambda i, k: (lambda f: f['C'][i] == k))(i, k))
    # ---- row / column aggregates
    for k in range(6):
        a('rowsused=%d' % k, (lambda k: (lambda f: f['ru'] == k))(k))
        a('colsused=%d' % k, (lambda k: (lambda f: f['cu'] == k))(k))
        a('fullrows=%d' % k, (lambda k: (lambda f: f['fr'] == k))(k))
        a('fullcols=%d' % k, (lambda k: (lambda f: f['fc'] == k))(k))
        a('maxrow=%d' % k, (lambda k: (lambda f: max(f['R']) == k))(k))
        a('minrow=%d' % k, (lambda k: (lambda f: min(f['R']) == k))(k))
        a('maxcol=%d' % k, (lambda k: (lambda f: max(f['C']) == k))(k))
        a('mincol=%d' % k, (lambda k: (lambda f: min(f['C']) == k))(k))
    a('eqrows', lambda f: len(set(f['R'])) == 1)
    a('eqcols', lambda f: len(set(f['C'])) == 1)
    a('hasfullrow', lambda f: f['fr'] > 0)
    a('hasfullcol', lambda f: f['fc'] > 0)
    a('allrowsused', lambda f: f['ru'] == 5)
    a('allcolsused', lambda f: f['cu'] == 5)
    # ---- the four corners
    for k in range(5):
        a('corners=%d' % k, (lambda k: (lambda f: f['co'] == k))(k))
    for i, nm in enumerate(('tl', 'tr', 'bl', 'br')):
        a('corner_%s' % nm, (lambda i: (lambda f: f['cs'][i]))(i))
    a('cornerssame', lambda f: f['co'] in (0, 4))
    a('anycorner', lambda f: f['co'] > 0)
    a('nocorner', lambda f: f['co'] == 0)
    # ---- blobs, lonely squares, touching
    for k in range(9):
        a('blobs=%d' % k, (lambda k: (lambda f: f['nb'] == k))(k))
    for k in range(11):
        a('maxblob=%d' % k, (lambda k: (lambda f: f['mb'] == k))(k))
    for k in range(1, 7):
        a('minblob=%d' % k, (lambda k: (lambda f: f['sb'] == k))(k))
        a('hasblob%d' % k, (lambda k: (lambda f: k in f['Z']))(k))
    for k in range(7):
        a('lonely=%d' % k, (lambda k: (lambda f: f['lo'] == k))(k))
    for k in range(13):
        a('touch=%d' % k, (lambda k: (lambda f: f['tc'] == k))(k))
    a('notouch', lambda f: f['tc'] == 0)
    a('alltouch', lambda f: f['lo'] == 0)
    # ---- the five symmetries a player checks by eye
    a('symlr', lambda f: f['sy'][0])
    a('symtb', lambda f: f['sy'][1])
    a('symhalf', lambda f: f['sy'][2])
    a('symdiag', lambda f: f['sy'][3])
    a('symanti', lambda f: f['sy'][4])
    a('sym4way', lambda f: f['sy'][0] and f['sy'][1])
    a('sym8way', lambda f: f['sy'][0] and f['sy'][1] and f['sy'][3])
    a('toprow=botrow', lambda f: f['tb'])
    a('leftcol=rightcol', lambda f: f['lr'])
    # ---- halves, the border and the middle
    a('abovebelow', lambda f: f['ab'] == f['be'])
    a('leftright', lambda f: f['le'] == f['ri'])
    a('moreabove', lambda f: f['ab'] > f['be'])
    a('moreleft', lambda f: f['le'] > f['ri'])
    for k in range(13):
        a('border=%d' % k, (lambda k: (lambda f: f['bd'] == k))(k))
    for k in range(10):
        a('middle3x3=%d' % k, (lambda k: (lambda f: f['ce'] == k))(k))
    a('midblack', lambda f: f['mid'])
    a('midwhite', lambda f: not f['mid'])
    # ---- shapes
    a('has2x2', lambda f: f['sq'])
    a('run3across', lambda f: f['hr'] >= 3)
    a('run4across', lambda f: f['hr'] >= 4)
    a('run3down', lambda f: f['vr'] >= 3)
    a('run4down', lambda f: f['vr'] >= 4)
    a('tworowssame', lambda f: f['rs'])
    a('twocolssame', lambda f: f['cS'])
    a('allrowsdiff', lambda f: not f['rs'])
    a('rectangle', lambda f: f['re'])
    a('straightline', lambda f: f['ru'] == 1 or f['cu'] == 1)
    return P


def FE(g):
    """Everything the outside pool reads off a picture, computed once."""
    R = [r.count("#") for r in g]
    C = [sum(r[i] == "#" for r in g) for i in range(5)]
    S = set((r, c) for r in range(5) for c in range(5) if g[r][c] == "#")
    Z, T = [], set(S)
    while T:
        q = [T.pop()]
        z = 0
        while q:
            r, c = q.pop()
            z += 1
            for p in ((r + 1, c), (r - 1, c), (r, c + 1), (r, c - 1)):
                if p in T:
                    T.discard(p)
                    q.append(p)
        Z.append(z)
    tc = sum(((r + 1, c) in S) + ((r, c + 1) in S) for r, c in S)
    lo = sum(not any((r + d, c + e) in S for d, e in ((1, 0), (-1, 0), (0, 1), (0, -1))) for r, c in S)
    gl = list(g)
    hr = max([max([len(x) for x in r.split(".")]) for r in gl] + [0])
    vr = max([max([len(x) for x in "".join(r[i] for r in gl).split(".")]) for i in range(5)] + [0])
    rs = [r for r in gl if "#" in r]
    cl = ["".join(r[i] for r in gl) for i in range(5)]
    cs = [c for c in cl if "#" in c]
    rr = [r for r in range(5) if R[r]]
    cc = [c for c in range(5) if C[c]]
    return {'n': len(S), 'R': R, 'C': C, 'Z': Z, 'nb': len(Z), 'mb': max(Z + [0]),
            'sb': min(Z + [0]), 'lo': lo, 'tc': tc,
            'ru': sum(x > 0 for x in R), 'cu': sum(x > 0 for x in C),
            'fr': R.count(5), 'fc': C.count(5),
            'co': (g[0][0] + g[0][4] + g[4][0] + g[4][4]).count("#"),
            'cs': [g[0][0] == "#", g[0][4] == "#", g[4][0] == "#", g[4][4] == "#"],
            'sy': [gl == [r[::-1] for r in gl], gl == gl[::-1],
                   gl == [r[::-1] for r in gl[::-1]], gl == cl, cl[::-1] == [r[::-1] for r in gl]],
            'tb': g[0] == g[4], 'lr': cl[0] == cl[4],
            'ab': R[0] + R[1], 'be': R[3] + R[4], 'le': C[0] + C[1], 'ri': C[3] + C[4],
            'bd': R[0] + R[4] + C[0] + C[4] - (g[0][0] + g[0][4] + g[4][0] + g[4][4]).count("#"),
            'ce': sum(r.count("#") for r in [x[1:4] for x in gl[1:4]]),
            'mid': g[2][2] == "#",

def RK(v):
    """(rarity-weighted total, plain count) of the surviving predicates a picture satisfies.

    The plain count is the direct port of the round-1 attack; the rarity-weighted total is its
    smarter sibling (RULE_FAMILIES.md sec. 5c).  The lineup aims the true candidate's rank on
    BOTH, so neither reading of "which of these four is most special?" pays.
    """
    w = v & RAREM
    t = 0
    while w:
        b = w & -w
        t += WTS[b.bit_length() - 1]
        w ^= b
    return t, v.bit_count()


# The sixteen (count rank, rarity rank) places the true candidate can occupy in its own lineup.
# One of them is aimed at uniformly per clue and the rest are tried in order of distance from
# it, so the realised rank spreads over all four places on BOTH readings instead of piling up
# at one end - which is what keeps "most predicates" and "fewest predicates" both at chance.
_AIM = [(a, b) for a in range(4) for b in range(4)]


def _isect(ex):
    """The outside predicates true of EVERY example - what an intersection player is left with."""
    C = (1 << NP) - 1
    for h in ex:
        C &= PP[h]
    return C


def _traps(ex):
    """The excluded rules consistent with EVERY example (bits 0..9), and the squares that are
    black in all of them (the 'what do they have in common?' trap, fitted to the clue)."""
    ct = 1023
    com = (1 << 25) - 1
    for h in ex:
        ct &= PT[h]
        com &= PB[h]
    return ct, com


def _slice(rr, L, k):
    """k pictures from L.  The pool itself was built in random order, so a wrapped slice is a
    random subset and costs a fraction of random.sample."""
    n = len(L)
    if n <= k:
        return L
    i = rr.randrange(n)
    return L[i:i + k] if i + k <= n else L[i:] + L[:i + k - n]


def _lineup(rr, j, ex):

    All four have the SAME number of black squares, fire exactly the SAME example-consistent
    excluded rules (revision 2 sec. 5b), and none is an example.  The true candidate's RANK is
    then aimed - on the plain count of the attacker's surviving predicates AND on their
    rarity-weighted total - so that "the candidate that fits most of my surviving predicates",
    which is the whole of the round-1 attack, is worth little more than a guess.  The second
    return value is 1 when at least one decoy beats the truth on both readings.
    """
    bit = BIT[j]
    ct, com = _traps(ex)
    C = _isect(ex)

    # only a stubborn one pays for the wide net

            # count-shaped traps ("at least / at most as many blacks as the clue", "the same
            # number as an example") are not in the key: all four candidates of a lineup have
            # the SAME number of black squares, so those three are matched for free.

            if len(ks) < size + 1:

                # only die if the examples disagree about the number of black squares

                       for i in range(size) for j in range(i + 1, size)):
                    continue                     # the examples never look like edits of each other

        # the coincidences a decoy can be built to carry, and they are the only thing that can
        # weigh as much as the hidden rule itself in a rarity-weighted reading of the clue.

        keep = None

            out, top = _lineup(r, rule, T)

                continue                         # exactly one candidate obeys the rule

def FT(g):
    """The 15-number readout of a picture; every rule of U is one of these == a constant."""
    R = [r.count("#") for r in g]
    C = [sum(r[i] == "#" for r in g) for i in range(5)]
    S = set((r, c) for r in range(5) for c in range(5) if g[r][c] == "#")
    Z = []
    while S:
        q = [S.pop()]
        z = 0
        while q:
            r, c = q.pop()
            z += 1
            for p in ((r + 1, c), (r - 1, c), (r, c + 1), (r, c - 1)):
                if p in S:
                    S.discard(p)
                    q.append(p)
        Z.append(z)
    g = list(g)
    return [sum(R), g == [r[::-1] for r in g], g == g[::-1], g == [r[::-1] for r in g[::-1]],
            (g[0][0] + g[0][4] + g[4][0] + g[4][4]).count("#"),
            sum(x > 0 for x in R), sum(x > 0 for x in C), len(Z), R.count(5), C.count(5),
            g[2][2] == "#", len(set(R)) == 1, len(set(C)) == 1, max(Z + [0]), Z.count(1)]


def UNIV():
    U  = [(0, n) for n in (5, 6, 7)]
    U += [(1, 1), (2, 1), (3, 1)]
    U += [(4, n) for n in (1, 2, 3, 4)]
    U += [(5, 1), (5, 2), (6, 1), (6, 2)]
    U += [(7, n) for n in (1, 2, 3, 4)]
    U += [(8, 1), (9, 1)]
    U += [(10, 1)]
    U += [(11, 1), (12, 1)]
    U += [(13, n) for n in (2, 3, 4)]
    U += [(14, n) for n in (3, 4, 5)]
    return U


def solve(clue):
    """Re-derive the survivor exactly as the scorer does and hand back the candidate that obeys
    it, verbatim.  Nothing is constructed, so there is nothing to leak."""
    X = clue.strip().split("\n\n")
    E = [b.split("\n") for b in X[:-4]]
    K = [b.split("\n")[1:] for b in X[-4:]]
    G = [FT(e) for e in E]
    V = [r for r in UNIV() if all(g[r[0]] == r[1] for g in G)]
    if len(V) == 1:
        for k in K:
            if FT(k)[V[0][0]] == V[0][1]:
                return "\n".join(k)
    return "\n".join(K[0])
